### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via validateScreenInputs (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 31260ca8e446fa4fbe94ff8fd2a9030ddfb53a9a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e8beaba8ef7c3cce37cd3732fdfb84523b30726c` — the merge of head `3eb877a57f96570eeaba79e7635a3f53056cdb49` into base `31260ca8e446fa4fbe94ff8fd2a9030ddfb53a9a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e8beaba8ef7c3cce37cd3732fdfb84523b30726c && git checkout e8beaba8ef7c3cce37cd3732fdfb84523b30726c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 31260ca8e446fa4fbe94ff8fd2a9030ddfb53a9a 3eb877a57f96570eeaba79e7635a3f53056cdb49 && git checkout -B drift-repro 31260ca8e446fa4fbe94ff8fd2a9030ddfb53a9a && git merge --no-ff 3eb877a57f96570eeaba79e7635a3f53056cdb49

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 31260ca8e446fa4fbe94ff8fd2a9030ddfb53a9a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 31260ca8e446fa4fbe94ff8fd2a9030ddfb53a9a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3eb877a57f96570eeaba79e7635a3f53056cdb49`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/screen-input-contract.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/screen-input-contract.test.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ScreenView.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ScreenView.boundHelpReference-9248.test.tsx (the narrowing-face floor: every non-prose path of the diff), and read in the cited code: packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (the resume door, `validateScreenInputs` call and the `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` envelope), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-nodes.ts (how `type` / `min` / `max` / `defaultValue` go on the wire), packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts (`INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` → 400), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/FlowRunner.tsx (`initialScreenValues`, `screenFieldBoundViolations`, `screenResumeValues` on submit), packages/spec/src/data/aggregation-policy.ts (`MEASURE_FIELD_TYPES`), content/docs/references/automation/builtin-node-config.mdx (the regenerated mirror of the `.describe`). Remainder at TIER_DEFAULT (the lane seat's ACCEPT): the two changesets, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx.

Inputs: card #30178 body and all six comments (triage `6641856071`, claim `6647305770`, needs_decision report `6647359070`, seat note `6647378538`, ruling `6648655128` letter A, done report `6649598953`); PR #30269 body, file list and the net diff against `main` at the head (merge base `797f9257`); the check-runs on the head. Ruling-ref on the PR body: `6648655128` ✓.

Gate verdicts (the head's check-runs, read at 2026-11-05T04:48Z): 65 check-runs, **58 success, 0 failure**, 7 skipped (the opt-in harnesses `18.x upgrade harness`, `Packed-tarball smoke`, `Temporal Conformance`, `UI Published Artifacts`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the unexpanded dogfood matrix placeholder, and the schedule gate). Green by name: `Type Check UI` (the Console compiled against this PR's spec and the `percent` line — the reading the dev left to CI), `Type Check · workspace` (the spec artifact gates, so the regenerated `builtin-node-config.mdx` is current), `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Build Core`, `Test Core (1–8/8)`, `Test UI (1–16/16)`, `Lint UI`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (the changeset gates, `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` among them), `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Resume-door accept set narrows** — a present value under a `type: 'currency'` or `type: 'percent'` screen field that is not a finite JSON number is refused `invalid_type` inside `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` (400, retryable, suspension kept: the door returns the envelope before anything is consumed, engine.ts resume path), never coerced. **Right** — ruling A item 1, the same `isFiniteNumber` predicate and the same `must be a number` sentence `number` carries; `"75"`, `"60"` and `"abc"` all land on the shape, a JSON number still reaches the bound pass.
2. **Not widened** — `rating`, `slider`, `progress`, `text` and untyped fields still admit a string (pinned). **Right** — ruling A item 1 ⛔.
3. **Console** — `percent` takes the numeric input path with `number` / `currency`: native `min` / `max`, the existing `Number(e.target.value)` posts a number, `screenFieldBoundViolations` (present finite number only) now sees it. **Right** — ruling A item 3, one line, one pin, no dedicated percent widget. `ui/` surface is exactly `ScreenView.tsx` and its existing bound harness; no other `ui/**` path moves.
4. **Error-code surface** — no new code: `invalid_type` is already a `FieldErrorCode` member and already the code `number` uses. **Right** (ADR-0114 D2).
5. **Published spec** — `ScreenFieldConfigSchema.type` stays `z.string().optional()`, `.min` / `.max` stay `z.number().optional()`; `ScreenFieldSpec` keeps every member and type. Only TSDoc and the `type` `.describe()` change, so `check:docs` is the one owed artifact gate and `content/docs/references/automation/builtin-node-config.mdx` is regenerated (both tables that carry the field row). No export moves, so `gen:api-surface` is not owed. A grep of the whole tree at the head for the previous describe sentence finds no stale copy. **Right.**
6. **Headless path (implied, not named in the PR body)** — `judgeHeadlessScreen` shares `validateScreenInputs`, so a caller-supplied string under a `currency` / `percent` field now yields `invalid_type` → `satisfied: false` → the screen pauses instead of being skipped on a value the bound never judged. Failure direction is the module's standing one (a pause, never a skip). **Right**, and the same behaviour `number` has had since A′.
7. **Metadata protocol unchanged** — what an author may write (`type: 'percent'`, `min`, `max`, `defaultValue`) is identical before and after; the narrowing is on a submitted value at the resume door. `Metadata-protocol: none` is the right declaration.

### ② Semver level

- Changesets: `30178-numeric-screen-fields-refuse-strings.md` (`@objectstack/service-automation`, `@object-ui/app-shell`) and `30178-screen-field-numeric-kinds-contract-text.md` (`@objectstack/spec`), both **`patch`**. By AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 and the launch-window guard's own rule (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: "the level follows the metadata protocol alone — `minor` when the protocol an author writes against is added to, narrowed or changed in meaning, `patch` for everything else"), `Metadata-protocol: none` ⇒ `patch`. **Matches.** The ruling's aside that A′ landed `minor` does not bind here: that landing declared protocol kinds, this one declares none.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` as a line-initial declaration on the PR body and in both changeset bodies, with the BREAKING banner in both and exactly one ADR-0087 marker each, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The exemption holds: no key, export or stored row moves, nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite, and neither body carries a FROM → TO prescription (the earlier draft's block was removed; the caller's fix is a plain bullet). **Matches.**
- `@object-ui/app-shell` is `private: true` but a member of the `fixed` group with `privatePackages.version: true`, so bumping it in the changeset is correct, and riding the service-automation changeset is fine (one changeset, two packages, one behaviour).
- Title `fix(automation)!:` carries the `!`; `Fixes #30178` on the body matches the changesets' `(#30178)`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` on the done report (`6649598953`) — nothing to escalate. The needs_decision fork (`6647359070`) was answered by the maintainer's ruling A (`6648655128`), and the diff implements that letter and no other: no coercion (B) and no engine-untouched arm (C).
- Deviation 1 (console pin in the existing `boundHelpReference-9248` harness as a top-level describe): accepted — the shared-harness rule.
- Deviation 2 (`@object-ui/app-shell` rides the service-automation changeset): accepted — see ②.
- Deviation 3 (`flows.mdx` changes three sentences, the ruling named one): accepted — the other two would have stated the `number`-only rule after this PR; same file the ruling opened; prose face.
- Deviation 4 (assignee / reviewer step skipped): seat process, no contract bearing.
- NOT MEASURED locally: `@object-ui/app-shell type-check` (unbuilt siblings) and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (whole-workspace build) — both answered by the head's check-runs (`Type Check UI`, `Build Core` / `Test Core`), read above.
- Dogfood: the one red (`permission-set-clone-door`) is attributed to main's own red; verified: #30255 is open and names that test after PR #30222, revert PR #30262 is open, and nothing in this diff touches permission sets or object registration. Accepted.
- Skills: `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`'s screen row names `type` as an open hint and states no numeric rule, so nothing there turns false. Accepted.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts`** — judged against ruling A and its first consumer, `validateScreenInputs` at the head. The `type` TSDoc's claim ("four members are value domains … the three numeric kinds take a finite JSON number, a numeric string refused and ⛔ never coerced; and `'file'`") is exactly the `SCREEN_FIELD_VALUE_DOMAINS` table: `number` / `currency` / `percent` on `isFiniteNumber`, `file` on `isFileIdToken`, exact-match on `field.type`. The `min` / `max` TSDoc's claim ("the shape refusal above reads the three numeric kinds alone, not the presence of a bound") is the code: the domain lookup keys off `type`, the bound pass is unconditioned on it. The `.describe()` sentence ("`number`, `currency` and `percent` take a finite number on resume (a numeric string is refused)") is true and is mirrored in the regenerated reference page. Shape untouched. Tried to break it: (a) case — the schema's `type` is a free string; the engine matches `'percent'` exactly while the console lowercases, so a `'Percent'` field renders numeric, posts a number, and the bound pass still judges it — no loss; a REST string under `'Percent'` passes unjudged exactly as it does under `'Number'` since A′, a pre-existing asymmetry this PR neither widens nor narrows and which the ruling did not open. (b) The widget hints `rating` / `slider` / `progress` — excluded and pinned, as the ruling requires. **Holds. No finding.**

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`** — `ScreenFieldSpec.type` now claims "the client renders all three as a numeric input, which posts a number": true at the head (ScreenView.tsx `htmlType` line and the `Number(...)` on the numeric input), and the client bound check compares a present finite number, so the claim and the gate are one change in one PR, which is the trap the ruling named (engine first, console later) closed. The `min` / `max` TSDoc ("a present non-number is refused outright (`invalid_type`) … ⛔ Not coerced") matches the pass order: shape before bound, absent and hidden left alone. Tried to break it: (a) a `defaultValue` served as a string on a numeric field — `screen-nodes.ts` resolves the slot as written and `initialScreenValues` seeds it as served, so an untouched string default would post a string and be refused (400, retryable). This is the author's off-spec declaration, identical to what `number` / `currency` have done since A′, and the spec text now says the field takes a number; reading the string as a number in the console would be the consumer leniency PD-12 forbids. Not a defect of this PR. (b) a whitespace-only string — `isPresent` is false, so it is `required`'s question, same as `number`. **Holds. No finding.**

**Non-prose floor** — `screen-input-contract.ts`: two rows plus a named predicate, the docstring's "one member / two members" wording becomes the three numeric kinds plus `file`; no new pass, no new code path. Its test pins every reading the ruling's item 2 lists (`"75"`, `"60"`, `"abc"` → `invalid_type` with the field named and `must be a number`; `75` → `max_value`; `-1` → `min_value`; `0` / `60` → `[]`; absent and `''` → `[]`; hidden / unevaluable not judged with the visible control; `rating` / `slider` / `progress` / `text` / untyped admit a string), for both kinds. `ScreenView.tsx`: one condition, one comment; its pin reads `type="number"`, `min="0"`, `max="60"`, `onValueChange('discount', 75)` with a number, and the bound check flagging it. **Holds.**

Observation (out of scope, not a finding on this PR): `judgeHeadlessScreen`'s inline comment "every issue returned here is a missing `required`" has been loose since A′ added `invalid_type` to the shared check; this PR widens that by two kinds but the verdict direction (pause) is unchanged.

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none.
